findings.why: The description of the bag piles up appositives (leather, monogrammed, expensive, 'the money in the grain and the weight of it') between subject and verb, so I lost the sentence's main action briefly.
The final clause 'the thing she had built her whole adult life around being looked at for' has an awkward stranded preposition that I had to re-parse to connect back to 'eyes'.
'a thing she said with a knife in it' and 'girls built to the one scale' are compressed metaphors I had to stop and unpack before moving on.

The phrase 'doing the thing her body knew how to do and finding it had stopped being the thing she was doing' is recursively self-referential and I had to re-read it to figure out what had actually changed.
The sentence ends on an abstract clause about her expression registering something with no name for it, which required extra work to connect back to the physical description before it.
A verbless fragment stacking three parallel 'where' clauses - I had to hold the sentence open without a main verb to land on.
A very long sentence chaining many simultaneous body-part observations across several dashes, making it hard to keep track of everything being described at once.
The referent of 'it' shifts from the bottle to the cap edge mid-sentence, so I had to backtrack to figure out what was being pressed into her thumbnail.
A new name, Daphne, is dropped in with a whole backstory implied but unexplained, so I paused trying to place who she was.
The self-interrupting parenthetical 'she could feel that she could not' inside the main clause made me lose the thread of the sentence and re-read it.
This compressed, abstract sentence about the face absorbing attention required slow, deliberate parsing to follow the logic.
The sentence is split twice by dashes and a parenthetical simile between 'Not tonight' and 'not ever,' so I had to re-read to reconnect the two halves.
